sections.heading: Known MOD structure in the current canonical reverse
items: The canonical MOD adapter validates the recovered 0x40 outer and 0x50 inner mesh grammar and materializes position, normal, fixed-point UV, BLENDINDICES-correlated and packed skin/control streams without treating unknown source bytes as disposable padding.

The recovered skin contract supports up to three serialized influences with 5-bit weights normalized by division by 31; the em000 corpus checks active bone references and preserves the raw source/control bytes as the authority for variants that are not yet fully decoded.

Hierarchy parent/order semantics, local-to-world transform composition and the inverse-rest skin-palette formula inverseRestWorld multiplied by currentWorld are promoted with executable-backed evidence, while motion-group values remain typed without inventing high-level names for every numeric value.

sections.heading: What MOD still does not authorize
items: Read-only structural and transform recovery does not authorize unrestricted MOD writing: broader revision coverage, bind and inverse-bind ownership, mutation quantization rules and original-game acceptance still require their own closure receipts.

A visible skeleton, decoded skin weights or a rendered model is not by itself proof that every MOD node is an animation bone, that every companion relationship is understood, or that a rebuilt document will be consumed identically by the original DMC3 runtime.

MOD-side animation binding is connected to hierarchy, motion-group and evaluated-local transform domains, but complete animation authoring remains coupled to the separately evidenced MOT decode/evaluator frontier rather than being silently absorbed into the MOD format page.

lessons.title: 01 — What is MOD?
lessons.description: Start with the role of MOD in DMC3 HD, its evidence boundaries and the difference between a model document, its runtime objects and neighboring resource families.

lessons.title: 02 — Document, objects and meshes
lessons.description: Walk through the recovered document/object/mesh organization and learn which structural relationships are safe to treat as typed data.

lessons.title: 03 — Skeleton, hierarchy and transforms
lessons.description: Study parent/order topology, local transforms, world composition and the evidence boundary between hierarchy nodes and higher-level bone semantics.

lessons.title: 04 — Skinning, topology and shader inputs
lessons.description: Follow packed skin influences, topology reconstruction and the shader-facing inputs recovered for the model family without flattening preserved control bytes.

lessons.title: 05 — Textures and materials
lessons.description: Relate MOD texture references and material-facing state to PTX/DDS resource identities while keeping model slots, extracted images and runtime textures distinct.

lessons.title: 06 — Animation and motion groups
lessons.description: Understand the recovered motion-group table, node-domain animation relationships and the boundary where MOT evaluation becomes a separate authority.

lessons.title: 07 — Related formats
lessons.description: Compare MOD with SCM, SHW, EFM, MOT and texture companions so shared concepts are not mistaken for identical physical formats.

lessons.title: 08 — Evidence and unknowns
lessons.description: Learn how DMC Rengine labels EXE-confirmed, corpus-confirmed, structural, candidate and preserved-undecoded MOD claims.

lessons.title: 09 — Reverse workflow
lessons.description: Use the project evidence workflow to move from raw bytes and corpus observations through hypotheses, implementation, tests and promotion gates.

lessons.title: 10 — Exercises and debugging
lessons.description: Practice diagnosing offsets, counts, hierarchy relationships, transform mistakes and skin/topology problems using evidence rather than visual guesswork.

lessons.title: MOD glossary
lessons.description: Reference the project-specific terminology used by the MOD reverse, including document, node, mesh, skin, transform and evidence domains.

lessons.title: MOD reference map
lessons.description: Jump from learning concepts to canonical code, tests, research notes and evidence packets that currently support each MOD claim.
